title: Recover failed dispatcher claims before external dispatch
description:
As an operator, I want a dispatcher claim whose broker publication becomes ambiguous to fail closed, so that a durable Procedure continuation cannot execute twice or remain indefinitely stranded in DISPATCHING.

Observed behavior: the dispatcher claimed a pending continuation, then its broker transport raised. The Task remained PENDING/DISPATCHING and could not be safely classified or reclaimed.

Feature: Fail closed after ambiguous broker publication

Scenario: Broker publication raises before acknowledgement
Given a pending Task has been atomically claimed by a dispatcher
When broker publication raises before returning an external dispatch identity
Then the Task becomes FAILED with dispatchStatus ERROR using a conditional update
And the failed dispatcher identity is cleared
And continuation metadata and sanitized failure evidence are retained
And the Task is not automatically requeued

Scenario: A delayed broker message arrives
Given a Task is already terminal after an ambiguous publication failure
When a delayed worker message for that Task arrives
Then the worker rejects it before invoking the Plexus command
And no duplicate Procedure execution occurs

Scenario: Dispatch was acknowledged
Given broker publication returns an external dispatch identity
When a later persistence update fails
Then the dispatcher does not rearm the Task automatically
And duplicate execution is prevented

Out of scope: GraphQL schema or resource changes; bypassing durable continuation checks; changing optimization policy.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Safety review refined the behavior: a broker exception may be publish-ambiguous, so automatic requeue is unsafe. The implementation will terminalize the claim with sanitized evidence and add a worker-side terminal-state guard. The currently interrupted local test run is recoverable separately because its captured error occurred during URL parsing before any broker connection.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Outside-in evidence: the broker-publication regression failed because the claimed Task was left without a compensating mutation. The delayed-worker regression failed because a terminal Task still proceeded toward CLI execution. The smallest fix now conditionally terminalizes ambiguous broker sends as FAILED/ERROR with sanitized evidence, never automatically rearms after acknowledgement, and returns a skipped result before command execution for terminal Tasks or unavailable claim authority. Focused validation: 25 dispatcher and worker tests pass.
